problems: The blind guess ('a stylised bird in flight, narrow body, angular wings spread left and right') matches the goose well. The kite/arrow alternative is a plausible misreading, because the right wingtip (22565) runs as a straight gold edge down to the tail tip (22957), which makes the outline read as a kite.

Star placement is mostly right: head/beak (23497) sits at the top of the neck at about (361,175), left wingtip (25945) at about (152,264), right wingtip (22565) at about (446,257), tail tip (22957) at about (413,420), and tail base (23607) at about (353,362) are all on the correct parts.
The breast star (23835, about (331,265)) sits on the wing-root line, not at the centre of the body. The body's visual centre is nearer (340,290).
The belly star (24010, about (315,357)) is on the lower edge of the body, which is acceptable.

The trailing-edge star (25278, about (208,302)) lies on the blue wing outline, but the trailing edge is only weakly defined, so the left wing reads as a thin triangle rather than a wing with a distinct rear edge.
The figure is upright: head at top, tail at bottom right, wings spread horizontally.
It is a real silhouette, not a copy of the gold lines: a blue outline of neck, body, wings and tail is drawn separately from the gold stick lines.

Label collisions: 'left wingtip (the leading fe...' is clipped by the body outline; 'belly, lower body' and 'base of the tail' overlap; 'head and beak, the top of th...' is truncated; 'breast, centre of the body' runs across the body outline.
Four unlabelled background stars (about (247,160), (84,325), (300,344), (442,397)) sit close to the figure and may be confused with key stars. The one at (300,344) is directly beside the belly star.
output.advice: Keep the composition, but tidy it. (1) Move the breast star 23835 from about (331,265) down to about (340,290) so it sits in the body's centre. (2) Strengthen the trailing edge of the left wing: draw the blue wing outline from 25945 (152,264) back to 25278 (208,302) and on to the body near (315,335), so the rear edge is a distinct curve. Do the same for the right wing from 22565 (446,257) back toward the body. (3) Stop the right-wingtip-to-tail-tip gold edge from defining the silhouette; either curve the right wing's trailing edge inward or shorten that line so the tail reads as a separate feature. (4) Shorten or relocate the labels: put 'left wingtip' above the wing, put 'belly' to the left of its star and 'base of tail' to the right, and abbreviate the head label to 'head & beak'. (5) Keep the unlabelled stars at (300,344) and (442,397) dimmer so they are not read as key stars. Verdict stays keep under the rule (match 4, fit 3), but the adjustments above would raise fit.
